question: Has there ever been a righteous person?
summary: Job 15:14, Isaiah 64:6, and Romans 3:10 deny anyone is righteous — all our righteousness is as filthy rags, there is none righteous, no, not one. Hebrews 11:4, 2 Peter 2:5-8, Ezekiel 14:14, Luke 1:6, and Matthew 23:35 name specific righteous people — Abel, Noah, Lot, Daniel, Job, Elisabeth, Zacharias. Same contradiction structure as id=35 but with 'righteous' instead of 'just.'

reconcile.connective: Defenders read "none righteous" as denying self-earned, sinless righteousness, while those called righteous are so by imputed righteousness of faith and relatively before men.

discrepancy.connective: The objection is pressed by Steve Wells in the Skeptic's Annotated Bible, who lists the flat "there is none righteous, no, not one" against the texts naming Abel, Noah, Job, Daniel, Lot, Elisabeth and Zacharias as righteous and asks whether there has ever been a righteous person.

pd_work.note: Gill treats this passage directly, harmonizing the 'none righteous' verses with the named righteous by distinguishing imputed righteousness of faith from self/works righteousness, and stating the righteous are 'not without sin, as none are.'

excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly harmonizes Noah being called 'righteous' (Gen 7:1) with 'none righteous' by distinguishing self/works righteousness (denied of all) from imputed righteousness of faith.
excerpts.source_note_text:
And the Lord said unto Noah,.... After Noah had built the ark, and got all things ready as were commanded him; and when it was but seven days ere the flood would begin:
Come thou and all thy house into the ark; that is, he and his wife, his three sons and their wives:
for thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation: this was a great character of Noah; that he was a "righteous" person, not by his own righteousness, but by the righteousness of faith he was both heir and preacher of; and this he was "before" God, in his sight, seen, known, and acknowledged by him as righteous; and therefore must be really so: and this shows that he was not so by the works of the law, but by the righteousness of Christ; because by them no flesh living is justified in the sight of God: and Noah was a rare instance of this character; there was none besides him in that wicked generation, so that he was very conspicuous and remarkable; and it was wonderful grace to him, that he should have this blessing to be righteous in an age so sadly corrupt, which was the cause of his being saved; for whoever are justified shall be saved eternally, Rom 8:30 as well as they are often saved from temporal calamities, see Isa 3:10.
